Word Woods audio credits

The starter story sentences, starter whole-word narration and four guide prompts were
generated with ElevenLabs, then levelled for tablet speakers. The game
plays bundled MP3s. The victory fanfare and five felt-piano score notes are original music for Readling.
https://elevenlabs.io

Later word collections
----------------------
The original twelve keep all their previous recordings. For later words, the
whole word and slow blend are two edits of the same human pronunciation.
The class shelf also uses short extracts from those recordings. Edits include
trimming silence, levelling, fading, pitch-preserving time stretch and MP3
encoding. PocketSphinx supplies alignment, not a synthetic voice.

The source of each recording is marked in /words.toml: a later word with no
voice field uses en_GB; en_US and commons select the sources described below.
Derived recordings retain the licence of their source.

GCompris / Art4Apps, British English pack: Art4Apps (Smart4Kids.com).
CC BY-SA 3.0: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/
https://github.com/KDE/gcompris-data/tree/5cfd4e4a4236701ec5e9d04a1796b6837d945403/voices/en_GB/words

GCompris, US English pack: Joshua Shreve, 2019. GPL version 3 or later.
See GPL-3.0.txt alongside this file. The complete original recordings used
for these edits are available under their word names at this pinned source:
https://github.com/KDE/gcompris-data/tree/5cfd4e4a4236701ec5e9d04a1796b6837d945403/voices/en_US/words
https://github.com/KDE/gcompris-data/blob/5cfd4e4a4236701ec5e9d04a1796b6837d945403/voices/LICENSE

Chip, plug, belt and trunk: Dvortygirl, US English, CC BY-SA 3.0.
https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:En-us-chip.ogg
https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:En-us-plug.ogg
https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:En-us-belt.ogg
https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:En-us-trunk.ogg

Extra story lines are rendered locally with the CMU Flite SLT voice.
https://www.festvox.org/flite/

Pictures: later words marked art = "woodcut" use illustrations made for
Readling. All other later cards use the GCompris words-webp collection,
copyright 2012 art4apps.org and 2022 Timothée Giet. CC BY-SA 4.0.
Readling fits each image to a square of cream paper and encodes it as WebP.
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/
https://github.com/KDE/gcompris-data/tree/5cfd4e4a4236701ec5e9d04a1796b6837d945403/words/words-webp

Original collection
-------------------

The letter sounds, slow blending models and fallback word recordings use
the sources below.

Most alphabet sounds come from Curious Learning's Feed the Monster Australian
English recordings. That pack also supplies cat, mat, bug and pig. The h sound
is the opening breath from the US English recording of hen. That recording
also supplies the whole word. The published English adaptation credits Curious
Learning, building on the original Feed the Monster project by Apps Factory,
CET and the International Rescue Committee.

Audio sources and attribution notice
https://github.com/curiouslearning/ftm-languagepacks/tree/7be4c9c922a6266b11f3f7821bb8ca6574f2cacd/AUSTRAILIANENGLISH/sounds
https://github.com/curiouslearning/ftm-languagepacks/tree/7be4c9c922a6266b11f3f7821bb8ca6574f2cacd/USENGLISH/sounds
https://github.com/curiouslearning/FeedTheMonsterJS#contributing

Curious Learning identifies the audio as Creative Commons Attribution (CC BY).
The source pack also carries the BSD 2-Clause notice reproduced below.
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/

Hat, dog, cup and sun are by Judith Franck and Association Shtooka, recorded
in British English. Their recordings are used under CC BY 3.0 US.
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/us/
https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:En-uk-hat.ogg
https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:En-uk-dog.ogg
https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:En-uk-a_cup.ogg
https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:En-uk-sun.ogg

Pot is by Commander Keane, recorded in Australian English. This recording,
including both adaptations bundled with Word Woods, is shared under
CC BY-SA 4.0.
https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:En-au-pot.ogg
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/

Pen and log are from Art4Apps (Smart4Kids.com, 2011), distributed by
GCompris. The original recordings are marked Creative Commons
Attribution-ShareAlike. The normal and slowed clips are also distributed
under that licence.
https://github.com/gcompris/GCompris-voices/blob/master/en/words/pen.ogg
https://github.com/KDE/gcompris-data/blob/master/voices/en_GB/words/log.ogg
https://github.com/gcompris/GCompris-voices/blob/master/LICENSE
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/

Edits for Word Woods include cropping, adjusting playback level, fading
clip boundaries and converting the audio to MP3. Some consonant endings
were shortened. The slow blending models each use one continuous word
recording, stretched in time while preserving pitch.

The audio studio also includes longer takes of b and d from the same
Australian English letter recordings. Each keeps the full spoken release,
with the surrounding silence trimmed. The studio identifies replacements.
